note: The captions for the Play listing's screenshots, and the layout each one is
composited with. `scripts/store-shots.sh` photographs the app on a headless
emulator and drops raw 1080x1920 frames in `.shots/`; `scripts/store-frame.py`
reads this file and turns them into the finished pictures.
The keys under `shots` are the ids in `src/shots.rs`'s SHOTS table, and they
have to be exactly those ids — `store/shots.json` and `src/shots.rs` are two
files in two languages joined only by these strings. Rename one on either side
and the shot it names quietly loses its caption, which is not a failure anybody
sees until the listing is live. So a cargo test asserts the two sets match in
both directions; see `the_listing_has_a_caption_for_every_shot_and_no_others`
in `src/lib.rs`.
Layout lives here rather than in the compositor because it is per-shot by
nature. `performance` is the clear case: its own screen already carries a title
across the top, so a caption sitting above it is two headings stacked, and that
shot wants its caption underneath instead. That is one word in this file rather
than a branch in Python.
Every key in `defaults` may be repeated inside a shot to override it, and only
the ones that differ are worth writing. `caption_position` is `above`, `below`
or `none`; `plate_scale` is the plate's width as a fraction of the 1080px
canvas; `plate_offset` moves it in pixels from the middle of the canvas (x, y,
positive down); `type_scale` multiplies the caption's size; the shadow is a
real gaussian blur in pixels, offset in pixels, opacity 0 to 1; `corner_radius`
is in pixels of the finished plate.
